notable_absence.finding: The sequence operators gate access with a single named RBAC privilege ('Query Use Sequences', granted on the scope), not with the disjunctive capella-role:* management-plane gate nor the Basic/Advanced credential-type pair seen elsewhere in this round's DDL/DCL statements. This is the same shape as server/'s named-privilege RBAC model (cf. privilege:query-manage-index), suggesting Capella's data-plane privilege model is not uniformly credential-type-keyed - some operations (like sequence use) are still gated by a discrete named privilege rather than the Basic/Advanced split.

cross_component_finding: Recurrence of the known docs-issue capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: this Capella page explicitly branches results by 'Couchbase Server 7.6-7.6.3' vs 'Couchbase Server 7.6.5' ('This query gives different results, depending on the version of Couchbase Server' / 'In versions of Couchbase Server prior to 7.6.5, the key is not regarded as part of the document...' / 'In Couchbase Server 7.6.5 and later, the entire VALUES clause...is regarded as a single document'), despite Capella having no discrete version numbers. Logged as a recurrence, not a new finding.
